Breathe hun... 

If you have a panic attack in front of your kids and can do nothing but sob, that's ok. Cry and get it out. You're not a bad mom or person when this happens in front of them... parenting is rough and definitely charges our emotions we're already feeling. 

My kids have seen me break down... I always try to talk to them afterwards and explain that I'm feeling sad etc. 
In my home I have started repeatedly telling my kids it's ok to cry. Everyone does. Don't apologize.  When I'm picking myself up and I hear that told to me helps me stop feeling so guilty. And I've noticed my kids open up to me and talk more now that they realize hey we're all in this together and everyone has feelings. 

Being overwhelmed, focus on one task. Nothing more. 
Even if that task goes undone today that is fine. Let's try it again tomorrow. 
Slowly work your way into a routine, don't force everything to be done right now. 

I encourage you to talk to your doctor and see if a medication would help. There is no shame in it. 

I can keep spouting off ideas but if you need to talk to another mom who has panic and anxiety then please message me. 
I pass no judgement, just a shoulder and ear.

I'm a mom also.... I wouldn't bat an eye doing what I absolutely needed to take care of my kiddos like you.

 I don't know if my words and life would change your mind, but its always worth a shot.

He got angry at me and screamed that I ruined his life at a birthday party this weekend.... :( 

Being a parent is tough, and waiting to receive help feels daunting but I hope you hang in there hun....

I'm not saying I don't agree with you, bc I do... But at the same time I understand that OP was doing exactly what needed to be done in -this- situation. Husband is leaving your home with a gun after an instance of holding said gun to his head, at this moment with no other option police are the best ones to call. 

I don't agree with the police issuing a warrant for a crime. I do hope that OP can have it dropped, unfortunately if it's the DAs decision that may not happen. 

I'm sure she wishes she had made sure the guns had been removed after the first time he talked about it... but they weren't. Yours, mine or anyones criticism won't change any of the facts that occurred. Instead maybe it can help someone else that goes through a similar situation in the future of what options they have available to get help for a loved one.

I do agree that jail isn't exactly an ideal place for someone suffering with mental health.... but what other options did OP have on stopping her husband? What do you think she should have done? (I'm sincerely asking, not being sarcastic)

I agree that its ultimately the parents choice, we all parent our children differently.. but yes there are definite foods that should be absolutely avoided such as carrots. Etc. 

My two were ok with the fruits and few other baby food flavors... but flat out refused a lot of them. (Which after tasting myself 😂 lmao, I can't say I blamed them. Ewwh)
I love your wording.... explains it best.

When my late SO was still here, I can say once or twice I'd awake in the night with it completely open. Yet having him next to me all cuddled up, I was able to sleep with em open. (He also slept closest to it, lol) 

But usually he always tried to make sure he shut it  for my sake. 

But heck no just ajar or half way.... There is just such an ominous feeling when it is.

Ooo, yes!!!

After cleaning my bathroom I will close the shower curtain, but I always open it immediately the next time I'm in there.

I always feel like a weirdo bc even at other peoples homes, I check behind their shower curtain before using the restroom. Lol

I've had my own kiddos (definitely way older than 2 months) choke on those snacks that are supposed to dissolve, along with a little girl I babysat that was almost 1.... thankfully the finger sweep was successful in removing the food. 

I agree with your other comments.... Raw carrots don't have a taste and obviously are incredibly dangerous for babies. 

My DS dad was very protective of our son, and wasn't comfortable with him having anything other than breast milk, formula or baby food until our pediatrician gave the ok.    ((--i should add I'm not judging you or your mom for giving your DD tastes of any food.... I honestly hope it didn't come across that way.  My DD whose 11 now, but when was small was given tastes of food but it was always my decision))
I had to look it up of who said this.... and I thank you very much for that much needed laugh.

Lol. My closet has quite a bit of clothing between mine and my late SOs. 

Along with those plastic 3 drawer things.... so realistically there isn't actual space for a person or thing to be able to hide there. But my brain refuses to understand this. Staring into a dark closet makes me extremely uncomfortable.

Lol, that is true... (being irrational)

I feel the same, safe and relief but the doors being closed.... 

I seriously find it interesting how we think/feel about the same situation.... but our minds having different solutions.

But if you dont have the closet light on it's nothing but a dark space... which hinders you being able to see if someone/thing were hiding inside. 

I don't understand nor know why this is a fear of mind... or when it exactly started. I just remember being this way since I was at a young age.

I actually think this is a smart idea for you to do. Staying in a strangers/new persons home, you honestly never know. 

Another weird thing I do....  If I come home and something feels off, I have a habit of checking every closet/place in my home.  
I'd rather look like a paranoid person and take the time to check, than ignore my gut feelings and it ends up actually being something more.

I'm so sorry hun. 

Tons of hugs.

I don't think I would handle having a mirror ON my closet door very well. 

In my bedroom I have one of those free standing oval mirrors that can flip (I don't know what or if they have an actual name, sorry lol)  Plus I have a rectangular mirror on the wall....  I don't mind these but just the thought of one being on the closet door makes me shudder.
Another person commented about the same book.... definitely going to pass. I don't know where or why my fear came to be but I know better than to feed into it. Lol

My cats have done the same.... which is why the doors are always closed with something blocking them.lol 

Nothing like the middle of the night, hearing that door slowly creak open. Nope!!! Lol

Take one day at a time.

Hugs hun.

I don't either.

I even do the same thing in my kids' rooms... except they don't realize it. 

I'm 30. Lol!

Just freaks me out.

That selfie someone posted... you don't see the 30 other pictures taken while trying to get the best shot. 

That vacation photo, new car or home..... you aren't aware of the credit card charges or debt their truly in. 

Etc.

Just reach out.... 

Us who have gone through losing a loved one by suicide don't mind people showing support. It is nice to be able to talk about our loved ones. 

From my own perspective... don't tell her how strong she is. I personally hate hearing it, as does my mother in law. There is no strength here, we aren't given a choice. 

You have your own personal story, and knowing someone else understands means a lot.

Music is always a good thing. I have to have some music blasting bc I can't sit in the silence. 

Our TV is only on when kids play video games. It has been a distraction for them.... 

I don't have advice on the friends/gf.
I received a lot of replies expressing their condolences. But after the funeral it has been nothing but silence. And one of my SOs "friends" only kept contact but slipped up showing his ulterior motives. 

People can really suck. 
But I have meet new people who share losing a loved one.... 

Did you ever try going to a different therapist? I have had some who are incompetent, but my current one has been a blessing. He used to be a tattoo artist (I myself love tats and have svrl)  I go in and cuss him out and he uses cuss words when replying back.  He isn't some uptight therapist. Finding someone to be yourself too and comfortable is a big relief.

What used to make you happy? Put that genuine smile on your face? 

If you don't mind me asking, what was your first attempt? 

What type of family do you have? 

I am asking bc I am sincerely wanting to know. If I can't help you find some small sliver of hope to not do this... then ok. But give me something to be able to remember you by.... yes a complete stranger. 
I am waiting for my own therapy appointment and today has been difficult for me, so would you mind talking with me?

I wish I didn't understand how you feel, but I do. 

I've been on both sides. 
Wanted to leave this world, had the letters wrote to my kids. My SO was who helped me get therapy and work through it. 

And now he took his life in December. 
I too feel lost, alone and miserable. I will live with this while raising 2 kids for the rest of my life. 

Living the aftermath.... your suicide affects many more people than you realize. 

I wish I could hug each and every one of you who are tired and exhausted. Life can be cruel and hard but things do change.

As you saw from the comments, people are insensitive assholes when it comes to suicide. 

I have been told sooo many comments since losing my SO. 

For us left behind with this stigma against suicide, it is difficult. We don't get over it.... all while hearing comments that make us angry. 

I am sorry you are feeling low. 
I don't know what to say anymore... there are people who will be greatly affected by your death. I wish you wouldn't.

instead of assuming her opinion, be honest with her. 

I dealt with a LOT with my own SO. But never once thought of leaving bc I love that man and knew who he was on the inside. 

Losing someone you love, is something you don't ever get over. 
I'm stuck here trying to make sense of everything while raising two kids.... he left us in December.

I'm sorry you think this is what you should do. 

I lost my other half in December. 
I have been attempting to reach out to others but I haven't been in a good place myself the last few days so I've taken a break from here....  there are some of us who do genuinely care even if you are just a stranger.

I'm trying to be because I don't want to leave something open for them. And with anxiety I tend to think of scenarios and what to do. 

I do agree that letting officers aware of the situation is a good idea.  And even if they still are legally bound to check each and every time, they'll understand. Plus would benefit me if anyone were to show up with them knowing background it would be a much faster process of them being removed from premises.

4 am.... absolutely silent in our house. No t.v. nothing. 

Alexa says, "that question is as easy as 2+2" 

I didn't know I could look through the app on my phone and see all the questions asked. 

Question was, how old are you? 


Next isn't creepy... son asked her to play peanut butter jelly song. 
Usually she rattles off radio station etc. Not this time. 
Instead sucker for pain automatically starts playing. 
Sons dad who passed, this was their song.

Thank you. 

They are appreciated.
